questions.text: Write a note on Kanakadasa
questions.text_as_printed: Write a note on Kanakadasa (Average )

answer.value:
Notes on Kanakadasa
Kanakadasa was a prominent composer of Dasara literature.
He was born in 1508 AD in Badagum village of Bankapura taluk.
His original name was Thimmappa.
Father: Beerappa, Mother: Bachamma.
He was the commander of 78 villages.
He was called Kanakanayaka because he was blessed with a golden (kanaka) container.
His ankita name was "Adikeshava".
He condemned superstitions.
In his compositions, he satirized the caste system.

Notes on Kanakadasa
Kanakadasa was a prominent composer of Dasara literature.
He was born in 1508 AD in Badagum village of Bankapura taluk.
His original name was Thimmappa.
Father: Beerappa, Mother: Bachamma.
He was the commander of 78 villages.
He was called Kanakanayaka because he was blessed with a golden (kanaka) container.
His ankita name was "Adikeshava".
He condemned superstitions.
In his compositions, he satirized the caste system.

He was called Kanakanayaka because he was blessed with a golden (kanaka) container.
His ankita name was "Adikeshava".
He condemned superstitions.
In his compositions, he satirized the caste system.

questions.text: Write a note on Mirabai
questions.text_as_printed: Write a note on Mirabai (Average )

answer.value:
Notes on Mirabai
Lord Krishna was Mirabai's deity of worship.
She is known as the "Radha of the Kali Yuga".
She was the daughter of Raja Ratan Singh of Rajasthan.
She was married to a prince of Mewar.
From childhood, she was inclined towards spirituality.
She spent her time in worship, meditation, and devotional songs.
Her husband's family opposed her devotion, so she left the palace and went to Brindavan, a sacred place dedicated to Krishna.
Giridhar Gopal was her deity of worship.
With hundreds of devotional songs, she remains eternal in the hearts of people.
